lstmnetvit_core_scaling.measurement_protocol: off/on/on/off/off/on: six full-output correctness-gated launches per core count, three per arm; two warmups and five timed inferences per launch; headline values are medians of the three launch means, not medians of the 15 raw iterations; eight-core affinity bounded to CPUs 0-7; performance governor at 1.6 GHz
lstmnetvit_core_scaling.executorch_protocol: fresh 2026-09-07 N=1/N=4 warm slopes; full correctness passed; exporter and runtime source both 7fc34bf6f53d2098e3e16c1fa71c23222f607330
lstmnetvit_core_scaling.finding: Replacing the four dominant grouped-im2col paths with direct grouped convolution, sharding their group dimension, serializing OpenMP regions below 10k static work units, prequantizing all 17 structurally eligible constant contraction weights AOT, and folding the 39 broadcast-to-named-add/mul chains that survive ordinary fusion cuts Merlin from 433.03 to a 130.880 ms launch median at one core and from 86.86 to 49.640 ms at eight cores. The targeted fold alone is 1.033x/1.027x in interleaved one/eight-core A/B. The distinct raw-iteration medians are 131.070 and 49.540 ms. Merlin remains 2.52x behind the fresh identity-matched ExecuTorch warm slope at one core and 3.23x behind at eight cores. The current arm scales 2.64x versus ExecuTorch's 3.39x, so both serial residual work and multicore efficiency remain open gaps.
